stopCondition.finding: A correct contract requires source/backing reads and destination writes to be intercepted across base/ring, far-star, debris, effect, and eventually pickup paths. The mandatory subset already crosses multiple fixed-placement segments; the complete Stage 2A character stack is a distributed compositor refactor. It cannot be placed without reclaiming another feature or changing transport/layout.

variantA.description: reuse the 19 projectile slot records; TOP address is stored, BOTTOM is derived through ring wrap, and existing BACKUP_TOP/BOTTOM holds latest underlay
variantA.lookup: linear scan of up to 19 physical slots; overlapping cells update the earliest/bottom painter owner
variantA.referenceHelperEstimateMethod: conservative instruction-byte count of a common 16-bit TOP/BOTTOM lookup plus ownership-aware load/store sketch; excludes claim/release and call-site growth

variantB.description: small hash/index or 140-byte physical-cell bitmap, while retaining underlay only in active projectile records
variantB.ramBytes: at least 32 B for a collision-handled hash index, or 140 B for one bit across divider plus 1080-byte ring
variantB.lookup: faster common negative lookup, but still needs exact-address validation, TOP/BOTTOM mapping, overlap ownership, claim/release code, and the same writer hooks
variantB.reason: adds state and code without solving fixed-segment hook placement; STOP forbids trying the second representation after the first requires a distributed refactor

staticAccessAudit.whyReadsMatter: A lower overlay that saves the visible projectile glyph as its backing creates a ghost even if its subsequent write is deferred. Ring copy likewise must copy logical underlay rather than the foreground glyph.

placementAtStop.finding: The helper alone exceeds the largest 90-byte local block before claim/release and hook growth. Splitting it among A2, ENTITY_CODE, PICKUP_CODE, and STARFIELD would require code compaction/relocation across the pipeline; PICKUP_CODE cannot grow because the fixed collision module must begin at $8FC9.
